# SPD-076 — Round trip: a level-2 heading inside a member's Brief becomes a section of its own, so test_acceptance fails on main

## Brief
Found on 2026-09-15 while recording SPD-065: `python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests -p 'test_acceptance.py'` on main fails twice in CutoverReadinessTest.

- `test_round_trip_differs_only_in_formatting`: re-rendering the imported committed ledger adds a blank line before `## Shared context` in ledger/teams/BADS-036/Marfona.md and ledger/teams/BADS-036/Roseval.md.
- The KNOWN_PROSE_KINDS check (tests/test_acceptance.py lines 66 and 389-391): the importer keeps `## Shared context` as a prose section of a kind it does not know.

Cause: the BAD-036 session planned those two members with a brief that contains a line starting with `## `. The CLI stores the brief as given; the render writes it under the member note's `## Brief` heading; the import splits the note at every level-2 heading, so the brief's own heading becomes a section, and the render then separates it with a blank line. Any brief, outcome, result or ticket prose containing a line that starts with `## ` hits the same break.

Decide and fix, with tests: either (a) the render and import delimit sections only by the layout's own headings (TICKET and member layout keys), so prose may contain any heading; or (b) the CLI refuses, or demotes, a level-2 heading in stored prose at write time, with a clear message. Prefer (a) if it keeps the disaster-recovery import exact. Existing rows must round-trip after the fix without editing Marfona, Roseval or Sarpo by hand.

Done when the full suite is green on main, and the three BADS-036 notes round-trip byte for byte.

A third row, found by the BAD-036 session (2026-09-15): BADS-036/Sarpo (02.01, scout) also has a brief with a line starting with `## `. All three briefs were written by nested parents (Amandine planned Sarpo; Superior planned Roseval and Marfona), and all three members are finished. The BAD-036 session left the rows untouched on purpose, so the fix must handle them as stored; no `member edit` rewrites of history. Add a scan to the tests that no stored prose in the fixture ledger breaks the round trip, whichever of (a) or (b) is chosen.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus in a worktree; small, but it touches how render and import delimit sections, so a reviewer on opus reads the diff before the merge.

## Outcome

Every command that stores ticket or member prose, plus import --file, refuses a line that is exactly an owned section heading, and the acceptance scan asserts no stored prose holds one.
